sources.entry: axolotl - A framework for fine-tuning and post-training large language models.

summary.one_liner: Axolotl is a free, open-source framework for fine-tuning and post-training large language models, driven by YAML configuration files.
summary.what_it_does: Axolotl runs full fine-tuning, LoRA, and QLoRA on many LLM and vision-language architectures from the Hugging Face Hub, including MoE models. It also covers quantization-aware training, preference tuning (DPO, IPO, KTO, ORPO), reinforcement learning (GRPO, GDPO), and reward and process reward modelling. A single YAML config can cover dataset preprocessing, training, evaluation, quantization, and inference. The README lists performance features such as multipacking, Flash Attention, Liger Kernel, FSDP2/DeepSpeed multi-GPU training, and Torchrun/Ray multi-node training. It can load datasets from local disk, Hugging Face, and cloud storage (S3, Azure, GCP, OCI). It also ships built-in documentation for AI coding agents via an `axolotl agent-docs` command.
use_cases: fine-tune an open LLM on custom data
LoRA or QLoRA training on a single GPU
preference tuning with DPO or ORPO
GRPO reinforcement learning for language models
export fine-tuned models to GGUF for llama.cpp or Ollama
how_to_run: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh (install uv; the README link is truncated, so this URL is inferred)
notable: YAML-driven pipeline that reuses one config from dataset prep through training, evaluation, quantization and inference
Broad training-method coverage, including QAT, NVFP4/MXFP4 MoE LoRA, GRPO/GDPO, and DFT-style loss options
Context and expert parallelism options (Ulysses, ring/USP, EP, N-D parallelism) for long-context and MoE training
Ships docs for AI coding agents through the pip package
caveats: Requires an NVIDIA Ampere-or-newer GPU for bf16 and Flash Attention, or an AMD GPU; needs Python 3.12+ and PyTorch 2.13+
Several advanced features are tied to specific hardware or setups (for example NVFP4 and NVLink/PCIe expert parallelism), so support varies by environment
The README says telemetry is enabled by default and can be disabled with AXOLOTL_DO_NOT_TRACK=1
